produced_by: bench/probe_block_propagation.py, compared by hand; see CHANGELOG 0.98.0
what: whether the merged upstream Sol-Attn kernel (Comfy-Org/comfy-kitchen#117, dae00a1) reproduces the branch build (0.2.31+sol.23d1a66) this repo's numbers were measured on
why: the merged kernel reshaped the API -- centroid_tail, reuse_qkv_memory and max_blocks are gone from both entries, tail/block_len/coarse_gate arrived -- so the node had to change to call it, and every Sol figure in this repo was taken on the older build
graph: h3_text_to_video_api.json, 4 steps euler, seed 730451892, Sol windowed to the final step, dense_blocks 0-48 so Sol runs at block 49 alone

comparisons.name: control: branch against branch
comparisons.arms: b49 19:39 and b49 22:32, same kernel, three hours and a server restart apart
comparisons.reads: the pipeline is deterministic, so any difference below is caused by the thing that changed

comparisons.name: baseline across the swap
comparisons.arms: sage at all 50 blocks, NO Sol node in the graph, 22:29 branch against 22:39 merged
comparisons.reads: the non-Sol path is untouched by the kernel swap. This is what makes the next row attributable to the Sol kernel rather than to the restart, the rebuild or the node edit

comparisons.name: Sol arm across the swap
comparisons.arms: Sol at block 49 only, 22:32 branch against 22:42 merged
comparisons.reads: the two kernels agree to about 1e-4 relative, not bitwise. Audio is unchanged because those rows ride the exact sink path rather than the routed one

conclusion: The merged kernel is NOT bit-equivalent to the branch build, and agrees to rel L2 7.67e-05 on the output latent -- roughly four orders of magnitude below the 0.0128 single-block effect this harness measures, and below every Sol figure in this repo. Existing measurements are not invalidated; a number quoted to more than three significant figures across the two builds is.
caveats: One graph, one seed, one block, one step count.
This compares OUTPUT LATENTS after a 4-step sample, not the kernel's own output at the call. A per-call comparison on captured activations would bound it tighter.
It says nothing about the merged kernel's NEW capabilities (tail=False, block_len, coarse_gate, the chunked QKV producer), none of which the vendored node exposes yet.
